strings.string: Involute gears sized for the nozzle that will print them. Pick a point for one gear or a pair, pick several for a gear train.
Select points for the gear axes
One point gives a single gear, or a meshing pair. Several points give a train: the first point is the input, the last one the output. All points have to lie on one plane parallel to XY.
Module = nozzle * factor. 2.5 is the sensible default: it puts about five extrusions across the tooth root, which is what stops a printed tooth shearing off. 2.0 is the fine end, 3.0 the sturdy end.
Total play between two meshing gears. Each gear gives up half of it, so a pair ends up with exactly this much. 0.25 mm suits most printers; go up if your parts come out over size.
Helical gears run quieter but push sideways on the shaft. Herringbone cancels that push and prints without support - the usual choice for a printed gear.
20 degrees is standard. 25 gives thicker, stronger tooth roots at the cost of a little smoothness, which is often worth it in plastic.
Below about 17 teeth the flank is undercut and the root goes thin. Profile shift fattens those teeth back up and the centre distance is corrected to match.
Reduction from the first gear to the last one. In a train the gears in between only reverse the direction, so the ratio is set by the two ends; the idlers are sized to reach the points you picked.
Puts a mating gear against the first one, at the correct centre distance for the ratio and the backlash.
Where the second gear sits, measured from the X axis. 180 degrees puts the two in a straight line, 90 degrees puts them round a corner.
Shaft hole through every gear. 0 leaves them solid. It is cut after the body, so a helical gear still gets a straight bore.
The tooth counts that reach your points do not give the ratio you asked for.
Gears placed on the points do not mesh at the ideal distance; play will vary.
A gear is so small that its root circle is barely above the shaft.
A gear twists more than half a turn over its width - narrow the face or reduce the helix angle.
Teeth would come to a point, so the tips are cut back to one extrusion width.
Select at least one point for a gear axis.
The module must be greater than 0.
The face width must be greater than 0.
The ratio must be greater than 0.
That much backlash leaves no tooth at this module.
A gear needs at least {0} teeth.
The pressure angle has to be between 10 and 35 degrees.
The helix angle has to be between 0 and 80 degrees.
The points are at different heights. Gears can only mesh on one plane.
Two points are too close together for gears of this module.
The bore is too big for the smallest gear in the train.
The tooth outline did not close into a usable profile.
This document is a part design and can only hold one component, so the gears were made as bodies instead. For one component per gear, create the design as an assembly.
